text:
incident-bot: Pager alert -> KV-cache continuous-batching tail latency spike (us-west-2). Affected models: mistral-7b-gqa, qwen-7b-mqa. Error rate up 4x, 95p latency > 10s. alerts:kv_batch_tail_high

sara oncall: ack. paging in. I’m oncall for next 6h. assigning to runtime and ml.

vivek runtime: looking at shard logs now. seeing bursty eviction + batch growth loops. suspect continuous-batching windows blowing up when prefix_len > 512 on MQA path.

aline ml: +1 saw similar in canary last week but small footprint. sounds like GQA/MQA interaction with prefix KV keys causing repeated cache misses and big batches.

ben sre: I’ll throttle batch max to 8 for the affected pool (us-west-2 / kv-pool-3). doing hotfix via infra API.

ben sre: command: `curl -X POST "https://infra-api.internal/pools/kv-pool-3/config" -d '{"max_batch":8, "enable_continuous":false}'`

deploy-bot: deploy started for pool/kv-pool-3 config change (run id: r-20260315-402).

vivek runtime: pushing a runtime dump to s3: `s3://redwood-inference/debug/1912345678/runtime-dump.log` — logs show continuous_batch.size climbing to 512 then immediate eviction events. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T03:21:02Z] batch_window=1024 active_batches=3 total_tokens=98304
[2026-03-15T03:21:03Z] kv_evictions=184 free_mem=420MB
[2026-03-15T03:21:04Z] tail_latency_ms=12450 requests=120 errors=6
```

aline ml: that aligns. MQA models keep context sharded, so batch grouping keys differ; with long prefixes the prefix hash distribution becomes sparse and we end up with large continuous batch queues. disabling continuous batching for MQA paths should stop growth immediately.

emily support: FYI support tickets from two enterprise customers in us-west-2 reporting degraded generation times and timeouts. IDs: C-9981, C-9984. Not yet escalated to customers but they are noticing.

sara oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle max_batch to 8 (ben) 2) disable continuous batching on mqa/gqa pools (ben) 3) revert any recent agent-side config pushes that increased batch window (if any) 4) set temporary rate-limit for affected models for hosted API keys to reduce pressure.

vivek runtime: I’ve applied throttle and disabled continuous batching on kv-pool-3. Observability note: we need to patch the controller to avoid re-enabling continuous when eviction_ratio > 0.2.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded for r-20260315-402.

ben sre: rolling restart of worker nodes in kv-pool-3 scheduled, staggering 2 at a time.

nathan product: can we quantify affected qps and which SKUs? we need to prepare a customer-facing note if SLA breach confirmed.

vivek runtime: initial estimate: ~8% of total hosted generation qps in us-west-2 for these model variants. Dedicated customers: 3 on kv-pool-3 (enterprise-tier) — might see degraded p95.

aline ml: root cause hypothesis: continuous-batching window controller doesn't account for MQA sharding causing pathological batch grouping across many unique prefix keys; when prefix length distribution shifts (longer system prompts + tool-calls) we hit a cycle where batches grow, fail eviction, then regen.

ben sre: temporary guard added to controller: `if model.meta.mode in ["mqa","gqa"]: continuous_enable=False` until we ship safe algorithm. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4512

emily support: ticket update drafted: "We're investigating intermittent latency increases for certain models in us-west-2. We're applying mitigations and will follow up within 2 hours." — want approval to send?

sara oncall: yes, send. keep tone brief, no technical details. escalate if we see SLO breaches.

vivek runtime: monitoring shows 95p tail down from 12s -> 900ms after throttle/disable. error rate back to baseline.

ben sre: worker restarts finishing, node-7 failed health check and was cycled. no data loss.

deploy-bot: health-checks passing for kv-pool-3 (6/6).

nathan product: good. note for postmortem: enumerate customers affected, timeline, mitigations, and a runbook change to detect batch window growth early. owner: aline ml, sla check owner: emily support.

aline ml: will own postmortem. immediate follow-ups: 1) add eviction_ratio alert for MQA/GQA 2) add unit test that simulates many unique prefix keys to ensure continuous batching stays bounded 3) design smarter grouping (prefix-aware)

ben sre: I’ll create a follow-up ticket for infra to add a safety throttle in edge controller. link: https://tickets.internal/RED-2789

emily support: sent customer note at 03:56 PT. two customers replied acknowledging. no escalations yet.

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. severity -> S2. start_ts=1912345678 mitigated_ts=1912345878.

sara oncall: handing off to next oncall @michael at 04:20 PT. leaving notes in pager duty.

michael oncall: ack handoff. I’ll monitor dashboards for 2h.

aline ml: postmortem ETA 2026-03-17 EOD. will include reproducer and code pointers.

ben sre: add me for follow-up on worker autoscaling behavior — looks like autoscaler reacted late.

sara oncall: thanks team. closing thread once postmortem link posted. :thumbsup:
